raw_segments.text: He sat down. I recalled his singular conduct of yesterday, and really I began to fear his
wits were touched. If he were insane, however, his was a very cool and collected insanity.
I had never seen that handsome featured face of his look more like chiseled marble than
it did just now, as he put aside his snow-wet hair from his forehead, and let the fire-light
shine free on his pale brow and cheek as pale, where it grieved me to discover the hollow
trace of care or sorrow now so plainly graved.
I waited, expecting he would say something I could at least comprehend, but his hand
was now at his chin, his finger on his lip. He was thinking. It struck me that his hand
looked wasted like his face. A perhaps uncalled-for gush of pity came over my heart. I was moved
